Risk factors for bronchiolitis obliterans: a systematic review of recent publications. J Heart Lung Trans- plant 2002; 21: 271–81. 15. Scott AIR, et al. Bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome: risk factors and therapeutic strategies. Drugs 2005; 65: 761–71. Pancreatic transplantation. Transplantation of the pancreas may be considered in some diabetic patients. In the vast majority of cases, pancreatic grafts have been transplanted together with a kidney (simultaneous pancre- as-kidney or SPK) in patients with end-stage diabetic ne- phropathy, which has produced better graft survival than transplanting the pancreas alone.1-3 However, pancreas transplants after renal allografting (PAK), or solitary pan- creatic transplantation (PTA), are becoming more com- mon,3 and approaching comparable survival rates.2,4 Ad- vances in surgical and preservation techniques, together with new immunosuppressants, have helped to improve survival.1 Overall patient survival has been estimated to be about 98% at 1 year, with graft survival of about 78%.5 The pancreas is a highly immunogenic organ, so extensive immunosuppression is required. Standard treatment often consists of quadruple therapy.2,6,7 Induction therapy is followed by maintenance therapy with a calcineurin in- hibitor (ciclosporin or tacrolimus), corticosteroids, and azathioprine or mycophenolate mofetil.2,7 Induction thera- py reduces rejection rates, and may allow for corticoster- oid withdrawal, but patient or graft survival is not al- tered.6,7 The use of induction therapy varies between centres,8 and may be dependent on the type of pancreatic transplant.9 The interleukin-2 receptor antibodies basilixi- mab and daclizumab are increasingly favoured. Rabbit an- tilymphocyte immunoglobulins are also used, but the use of muromonab-CD3 has declined.7 Alemtuzumab is under investigation.5 Tacrolimus is usually preferred to ciclosporin2-4,6,7,9 as it appears to allow for rapid tapering or even complete with- drawal of corticosteroids, causes less rejection, and may increase graft survival and reduce the risk of pancreatic thrombosis.
